novelty_flags.label: related_work; project_justification; novelty_justification
novelty_flags.one_line: Fenaroli2026 Section 4.2 does use never-treated controls and says not-yet-treated controls would require accounting for comparison-group anticipation, but the inspected source does not support the stronger claim that its Conclusion explicitly identifies that case as future work.

soundness_flags.label: ass:pt-all
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited CallawaySantAnna2021 conditions are limited anticipation plus conditional parallel-trend equalities for specified comparison groups, not the proposal's all-cohort additive mean restriction over every cohort-time cell; retag this stronger PT-All condition as novel and justify it.

soundness_flags.label: ass:bounded-anticipation
soundness_flags.one_line: Fenaroli2026 assumes bounded cohort-level anticipation increments with a particular sensitivity parameterization, not the proposal's edgewise bounded mean-distortion condition on contaminated reused controls; retag and motivate the latter as a proposal-specific sensitivity restriction.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Open-ended Question 1 and Theorems 4–6
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Causal sharpness and full-law endpoint attainment are conditional on resolving the announced-policy exhaustive extension property; the current handle is a concrete construction route rather than an assumed completion theorem.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The affine identified region and its sharp transshipment endpoints are claimed only UNDER a positive resolution of Open-ended Question 1; the cycle, bridge, feasibility, and mean-band targets remain unconditional.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper's staggered section fixes never-treated controls, imposes bounded cohort-level anticipation increments, and says that not-yet-treated controls would require accounting for anticipation effects in the comparison group.

source_verification_receipts.version: December 1, 2020 paper PDF corresponding to the Journal of Econometrics article
source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 7–10, Assumptions 3–5 and Theorem 1, PDF lines 254–275 and 486–527
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Assumption 3 is limited treatment anticipation; Assumptions 4 and 5 are conditional parallel-trends restrictions based respectively on never-treated and not-yet-treated comparison groups; Theorem 1 identifies ATT(g,t) under those conditions.
PIES proves sharpness by extending admissible lower-dimensional subdistributions to observationally equivalent full distributions, supporting the need for a separate completion argument here.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Retag PT-All and edgewise bounded anticipation as novel assumptions, then give an application-facing calibration protocol explaining how horizons and each interval are elicited or benchmarked; explicitly distinguish them from Callaway--Sant'Anna's clean-cell horizon and Fenaroli's increment bounds.

Replace the unsupported claim about Fenaroli's Conclusion with the exact Section 4.2 comparison: it fixes never-treated controls and observes that not-yet-treated comparisons require accounting for their anticipation.

Add a fully specified nondegenerate three-cohort observed-law exhibit through the announced-policy completion handle, including the potential-outcome mixture and endpoint-attaining full law if it succeeds; this would turn the conditional sharpness payoff into the unmistakable field contribution.
